observations: Two Nikon lenses are shown resting on bubble wrap.
The foreground lens barrel is marked '50mm 1:1.8G'.
The front ring of the lens is marked 'AF-S NIKKOR'.
Large black rectangular boxes are overlaid on all three images, deliberately obscuring parts of the lenses and background.
A watermark for 'OLAJIDE AMOS BISHOP' and 'POSTED ON JIJI' is visible across the center of the images.
The exterior of the lenses appears clean, but the internal glass and mechanical components are not fully visible.

claims.evidence: Internal glass condition and mechanical functionality cannot be confirmed from these photos.

risks.risk: Internal fungus, haze, or heavy dust
risks.proof: A clear photo looking through the lens elements against a bright light source.
A video clip showing the lens successfully and quietly autofocusing on a compatible camera body.

risks.risk: Scratches or coating damage on the rear glass element
risks.proof: A clear, close-up photo of the rear lens element and mount.
risks.if_unproven: as having a damaged rear element

proof_requests: Original, unedited photos without black redaction boxes.
Photo of the rear glass element.
Photo looking through the lens against a light to check for fungus.
Video of the lens autofocusing on a camera body.
response.reason: The presence of large, deliberate black redaction boxes in every photo is a strong indicator of stolen imagery used to hide original watermarks or identifying marks. The visible watermark also suggests the photos belong to a different individual.
